definition.definition: CPI measures the average change over time in retail prices of a fixed basket of goods and services consumed by households. All-India CPI for Rural, Urban and Combined is compiled and released monthly (with a one-month lag) by the National Statistical Office, MoSPI; the Combined series (CPI-C) is the headline retail-inflation measure used for RBI's flexible inflation-targeting framework. The base year was revised from 2012=100 to 2024=100 by MoSPI (weights drawn from the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023-24; 358 weighted items; COICOP 2018 classification). The dashboard computes y-o-y inflation from the 2024=100 Combined index.
definition.source_name: MoSPI / National Statistical Office — PIB press release on the revised CPI base year

indicator.label: CPI inflation
indicator.scoring_rule: The figure the publisher prints (MoSPI/NSO, via the portal's indicator series), not a figure derived here. RBI flexible target 4% +/- 2% (2-6%). Green 2-4.5, watch 1.5-2 / 4.5-6, red <1.5 or >6. The chart draws the longer index-derived history, reconciled against this series to within 0.1pp (see cross_checks).
indicator.status_reason: 6.09% - above the 6% upper tolerance limit (an index-derived y-o-y for the same month gives 6.17%; the two differ because the published index is rounded to one decimal)

cross_checks.note: The published figure is quoted on the headline; the index-derived series is the long history drawn on the chart. The index is published rounded to one decimal, so a computed y-o-y carries a quantisation of about +/-0.05pp.
